title: Multi-Exam Study Schedule Planner
promptText:
You are an academic coach who helps university students plan exam periods where several finals fall close together. My exams are:

[EXAMS]

How confident I feel in each course, and my weakest topics: [CONFIDENCE]

My available study time and fixed commitments: [AVAILABILITY]

I am starting on [START_DATE].

Please build my study plan:
1. Total the study hours I actually have before each exam, then show how you split them between courses and why, weighing exam date, weight in my final grade, and my confidence
2. A day-by-day schedule from the start date to my last exam, giving every session a course, a length, and a specific task rather than just "study"
3. Active recall for each course (practice questions, past papers, self-testing), including at least one timed practice exam under exam conditions per course
4. Spaced review, so each weak topic comes back at least twice before its exam
5. About 10% of my hours held back as buffer, and a lighter final evening before each exam
6. A short rule for what to cut first if I fall behind

Only use the hours I have listed. If they are not enough to cover everything, say so and tell me what to prioritize instead of overfilling the days.
description: This prompt has Gemini plan study time across several exams that fall close together. It totals the hours you actually have before each exam, splits them between courses based on exam date, grade weight, and how confident you feel, and lays out a day-by-day plan with a specific task for every session. The plan builds in active recall and a timed practice exam for each course, brings weak topics back more than once, holds back buffer time, keeps the evening before each exam light, and ends with a rule for what to cut first if you fall behind. It is meant for students facing finals week or a cluster of midterms, and it tells you when your hours are not enough instead of overfilling the days.

variables.name: EXAMS
variables.description: Each exam with its date, time, format, and weight in your final grade
variables.example: Organic Chemistry II final: Wednesday Dec 9, 9am, cumulative, 35% of grade. Calculus II final: Friday Dec 11, 2pm, 30%. Intro to Psychology final: Monday Dec 14, 10am, multiple choice, 25%.

variables.name: CONFIDENCE
variables.description: How you feel about each course and the specific topics you are weakest on
variables.example: Orgo: weak on reaction mechanisms. Calc: fine on integration, weak on series convergence tests. Psych: comfortable, just need to review.

variables.name: AVAILABILITY
variables.description: Hours you can study on each day of the week, plus fixed commitments such as work shifts
variables.example: 3 hours on weekdays, 6 on Saturdays, 4 on Sundays. I work Thursday evenings, so only 1 hour on Thursdays.

variables.name: START_DATE
variables.description: The first day of the plan

tips: List fixed commitments such as shifts, labs, and travel on the days they happen, not as a weekly total. A plan built on an average week breaks on the first unusual one.
Name weak topics precisely ("series convergence tests", not "calculus") so the plan can schedule them more than once.
Rerun the prompt halfway through with what you have finished and what you have not. A revised plan beats forcing the original one.
exampleOutput:
**Hours available:** 46 from Mon Nov 30 to Sun Dec 13. Assigned: Organic Chemistry 17, Calculus II 11, Psychology 11. Buffer: 4 (Sun Dec 6 and Sat Dec 12, 2 each). Left free: 3 (Dec 8, 11, and 13), for lighter evenings before Organic Chemistry and Psychology and a rest after Calculus.

**Why this split:**
- Organic Chemistry comes first, carries the most weight, and has your weakest topic, so it gets the most hours, all before Wed Dec 9.
- Only 4 study hours fall between your Organic Chemistry and Calculus exams, so 7 of Calculus's 11 hours come before Dec 9, mostly on series.
- Psychology is last, multiple choice, and your strongest course, so it gets short recall sessions early and most of the final weekend.

**Week 1:**
| Day | Plan |
|---|---|
| Mon Nov 30 | Orgo 2h: mechanism practice set 1 · Calc 1h: series convergence tests |
| Tue Dec 1 | Orgo 2h: mechanism practice set 2 · Calc 1h: series problems |
| Wed Dec 2 | Orgo 2h: redo missed mechanisms from sets 1–2 · Calc 1h: series review |
| Thu Dec 3 | Psych 1h: flashcard recall (fits your work night) |
| Fri Dec 4 | Orgo 2h: synthesis problems · Calc 1h: integration practice |
| Sat Dec 5 | Orgo 3h: timed practice exam · Calc 2h: mixed problem set · Psych 1h: flashcards |
| Sun Dec 6 | Orgo 2h: rework every practice-exam question you missed · Buffer 2h |

**Week 2:** Mon Dec 7 Orgo 2h, Calc 1h · Tue Dec 8 Orgo 2h light review, then stop · Wed Dec 9 exam, then Calc 3h timed practice exam · Thu Dec 10 Calc 1h formula and series review · Fri Dec 11 exam, then Psych 2h · Sat Dec 12 Psych 4h timed practice exam and review, Buffer 2h · Sun Dec 13 Psych 3h missed questions and flashcards, early night.

**If you fall behind:** spend buffer hours on Organic Chemistry first. If you are still behind, shorten Psychology's Saturday session, not Calculus.
